title: feat(auth): an invitation is accepted in one step with the proof its mail carries
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"zhuangjianguo"} -->
_Requested by **Steedos** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_018ETKaNwMZCNRYD7D8Q9Ubb?thread=cmsg_018ETKaNwMZCNRYD7D8Q9UbbSUQWB2j9eHYsRcrCiq1X1C)_

Fixes #34257
Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：邀请邮件里的链接带一个只在邮件里出现的凭证；受邀人一次提交（姓名+密码，或 Google / Microsoft 登录）就完成建号、邮箱验证、接受邀请和登录。新增公开路由 `POST /api/v1/auth/organization/accept-invitation-one-step`，客户端方法 `acceptInvitationOneStep`（`@object-ui/auth`），spec 可选键 `SendTemplateInput.deliverOnlyData`；这三个名字请在批准时确认。复制的链接不带凭证，仍走今天的流程。
- 为什么改：受邀人今天要注册、收验证邮件、再登录、再点接受，四步才能进组织（cloud#4470 依赖这一步，它运行在控制面、不在 `OS_CLOUD_MANAGED` 环境里）。
- 风险与回滚：新增一个公开的认证入口；它在 `OS_CLOUD_MANAGED=1` 时一律拒绝（409），自托管与控制面不受影响；原有路由和复制链接的行为不变。回滚即 revert 本 PR，已发出的邮件链接退回今天的登录流程。
- 先看：`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/invitation-mailbox-proof.ts`（凭证核验、各道闸门、`oneStepSignInState` 白名单式收口规则：只有逐项读到“除邮箱外别无凭据”才设密码，其余一律回答“去登录”；API 密钥与 OAuth 客户端授权同样算作凭据）；`packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/email-service.ts` 的 `sendTemplate`（只投递不入库）；`docs/adr/0138-…` 新增的一条修订。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run src/invitation-one-step-acceptance-34257.test.ts`，预期 66 个用例全绿。
- 需要你做的：批准 ADR-0138 本次修订对裁决 6413975861 Q2 B 的细化——带凭证的邮件链接即证明邮箱，复制的链接仍需验证邮件；同时确认上面三个新名字。

## What changes

- **The invitation mail carries a mailbox proof.** Each invitation mail's accept link carries a single-use proof bound to the invitation, its address and its expiry, handed to the mail as a deliver-only value; a resend retires it. The proof is never at rest in clear, the stored mail row never holds the proof, and the copy-link action answers the link without it. A send whose proof cannot be issued still goes out, as today's link. The invitation mail is sent inline, never queued, because the queue delivers from the stored row.
- **`SendTemplateInput.deliverOnlyData`** (`packages/spec/src/contracts/email-service.ts`, a spec contract widening, owed review at the contract tier). Render values delivered with the message and never written to the stored mail row, which gives no sign they were overlaid. Required template variables are checked against `data` alone. A send carrying them is delivered inline, never through the durable queue, so its sender gives up queued delivery where a queue is mounted. Only the server-side template send declares the key: `POST /email/send` and a script's `ctx.email.send` take a `SendEmailInput`, which has none.
- **One door redeems it**: `POST /api/v1/auth/organization/accept-invitation-one-step` (route ledger row, mounted-surface entry, envelope declaration, rate-limit rule and breach-check path list).
  - Rate limit first, per client network address and per invitation (10 per 60 s, `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`).
  - Proof mode: on a cloud-managed environment (`OS_CLOUD_MANAGED=1`) every request carrying a proof answers the cloud-managed refusal, `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, before the proof is read. Elsewhere the invitation must be pending and the proof must be the one issued for it, its address and its expiry. A bad proof gets one `INVALID_TOKEN` refusal that does not say which check failed, and the real proof stays usable.
  - The closing rule for an existing account: the door sets a password on an existing account only when it reads that the mailbox is the account's one claim: the address is not verified, the account's only sign-in account is its email and password one or it has none, it has no second factor, no verified phone number, no API key and no OAuth client consent, its identity source is local, and the server allows a local password here (not SSO-only, email and password on). Every other account, including one in a state no rule names, answers `sign_in`, and the proof stays unspent.
  - The judge (`oneStepSignInState`) is an allow-list: it lets the password be set only when every value it reads is positively the one that carries no other claim. A value no rule names (a stored flag in a form it does not read, an identity source no rule names) answers `sign_in` as `unrecognised`, never a pass. Its reasons are one exported list (`ONE_STEP_SIGN_IN_STATES`, now thirteen: the eight before, `verified_phone`, `api_key`, `oauth_consent`, `grant_unreadable` and `unrecognised`), and the test holds one case per reason.
  - Standing grants (API keys, OAuth client consents) count as claims. The door reads, on the existing-account path only, whether the user holds any `sys_api_key` row and any `sys_oauth_consent` row, revoked or not, each by one indexed lookup on `user_id` (`readStandingGrant`). Any row answers `sign_in` (`api_key`, `oauth_consent`). A table that does not exist holds no rows; a read that fails answers `sign_in` as `grant_unreadable`.
  - The sign-up gates run before anything is written: email sign-up switched off (and SSO-only mode, which forces it off) for a new address, password length, complexity, breach check, a name for a new account, and the audience admission. A refused request writes nothing and leaves the proof usable.
  - The proof is spent only by a request that passed every gate. One server process serializes concurrent redemptions of a proof, so exactly one succeeds; across server processes single use is as strong as the store's consume (see Acceptance notes). Then the account is created, or an unverified account gets the typed password and loses every session, each recorded with the reason a password reset records; the password-age stamp and the forced-change clear are written (ADR-0069 D1); on an account whose password it replaces, the password history is consulted before the proof is spent (a reused password answers `400 PASSWORD_REUSE` with the proof unspent) and extended after, as the reset door does; the address is verified, a session is issued, and the invitation is accepted.
  - Session mode (no proof, the provider return): accepts only when the session's address is the invited one and verified, otherwise answers `verify_email`.
- **`cloud-managed.ts` and `sso-only-local-password.ts`** name the door among the password doors; `CLOUD_MANAGED_REFUSAL_MESSAGES` gains the door's message. **`session-tombstone.ts`** ledgers the door with `password_reset`.
- **ADR-0138 D2 note** (the single authorized note): the door's rules; the anonymous `GET /api/v1/auth/oauth2/client-name` read that #34265 adds (#34168), with its 404, 400 and 429 answers; and the refinement of ruling 6413975861 Q2 B, which the note states awaits the maintainer's approval on this Tier H hand-off.
- **Anonymous door sweep** (`packages/qa/dogfood/test/anonymous-door-sweep.classification.ts`): class 2 gains the client-name read by its route, and the one-step door as a door the auth catch-all serves, probed by its own path and held to the class's answer.
- **`@object-ui/auth`**: `acceptInvitationOneStep(input)` on the client, the context and `useAuth`, with the types `AuthInvitationOneStepInput` and `AuthInvitationOneStepOutcome`.
- **Accept page**: a signed-out visitor whose link carries the proof sees one form, a name and a password, or a provider sign-in, in place of the sign-in redirect. The accept page does not keep the proof in its address. On acceptance the page shows the joined state, and Continue enters the organization as it does today. A provider sign-in returns to the page, which redeems the invitation for the new session. A link without the proof keeps today's path. Eleven new `organization.accept.*` keys in every pack (zh-Hant generated).

## Tests

New tests, in card-named files; every test name states a rule:

- `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/invitation-one-step-acceptance-34257.test.ts`: 66 tests over a real `AuthManager` and a memory engine. Every gate the changeset names has a case asserting status and code (or the `sign_in` outcome), that the tables a redemption writes are unchanged, and that the same proof is redeemed afterwards: sign-up off, SSO-only (new address), password length, complexity, breach, audience admission, missing name, the per-client-address window, the cloud-managed refusal, and each of the thirteen reasons of the closing rule (a table typed over the exported list, with a completeness pin), including the accounts outside the eight earlier states: one with a verified phone number, one whose identity source no rule names, one holding an API key (a revoked one), one holding an OAuth client consent, and one whose grants cannot be read, each answering `sign_in` with nothing written and the proof unspent, and accepted once it leaves that state. A grant table that does not exist holds no grant: that account is accepted. The judge itself has a table: the one allowed reading sets the password, and one step off it on each value it reads answers its reason, including a stored flag in a form it does not read (`unrecognised`), an API key, an OAuth client consent, and either grant reading unreadable. The password history: a password in the history answers `PASSWORD_REUSE` with nothing written and the proof unspent, and the replaced hash is recorded after acceptance. Also: two concurrent redemptions accept exactly once; the password-age stamp and forced-change clear in both modes; the revoke reason on the ended sessions; the breach-check list against the installed vendor default; the anonymous session-mode refusal's `UNAUTHENTICATED` code.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/send-template-deliver-only-34257.test.ts`: 3 tests.
- `ui/packages/auth/src/__tests__/acceptInvitationOneStep-34257.test.ts`: 4 tests.
- `ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/organizations/__tests__/acceptInvitationOneStep-34257.test.tsx`: 10 tests.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.test.ts`: two plugin-list pins name the new plugin.
- `packages/qa/dogfood/test/anonymous-door-sweep.dogfood.test.ts`: one leg for the class-2 doors a catch-all serves.

## Acceptance notes

- Single use across server processes: the platform adapter's consume reads the proof row and then deletes it, which is not one atomic step, so two processes redeeming the same proof at the same instant could both pass. Within one process the vendor serializes the consume, and the concurrent pin holds that. The module doc, the ADR note and the changeset state the guarantee at that strength. Making the adapter's consume conditional on its own delete is a change to every single-use value the platform stores, not to this door. The follow-up is tracked in the security channel.
- If a write fails after the consume (the account create or link, the password update) or the vendor acceptance fails after the session is issued, the error is answered and the proof is already spent; the person uses the link without it, as today, and can accept from the page.
- The vendor `accept-invitation` route is unchanged; its narrowing is #34272.
- The client-name read came in from `main` (#34265) with this branch's merge of main; its class-2 row is read by the sweep.
- The copy-action pin is an equality pin: the proof is never at rest in clear, so no mutation short of planting new code makes the copy action carry it. It has no ablation leg.
- The audience-admission case sets an off-vocabulary posture behind the entry validation, which refuses one at the door; it is the one posture that refuses an invited address.
